scope: Full-coverage discovery and preregistered selection for the SDK / coding-harness / durable-runtime / sandbox-worker-runtime / dispatch-framework / protocol-SDK layers beyond Claude Code and Codex. Evidence class: source_review end to end (GitHub metadata, upstream docs, publisher release data) plus one native local_integration execution on the WSL2 host for the single integrate_now row; nothing here promotes a catalog layer verdict.
method: discover (12 finders, critic, gap round) -> gh metadata enrichment and gates -> 3-judge shortlist per category (majority) -> evidence packet per shortlisted repo (Sonnet) -> accuracy and fit refutation (Opus) -> 3-judge selection per category on preregistered criteria (majority; conservative on no majority) -> completeness critic
criteria: Preregistered criteria (apply exactly these, cite evidence for each): C1 native-auth fit: runs on the user's existing native sign-ins (Claude Code subscription login, Codex/ChatGPT login, GitHub login, Google login) or a local model; a separate paid API key is a recorded penalty, not an exclusion. C2 programmatic control: SDK or headless/exec mode with structured events, resumable sessions, custom tools or MCP. C3 isolation and ownership: works per worktree/sandbox without hidden global state; deterministic code can own the effects. C4 evidence quality: upstream tests and CI, release cadence in the last 6 months, permissive or source-available license recorded, maintenance signals. C5 non-duplication: adds capability beyond the incumbents; overlap without an executed comparison means keep_but_compare with a named comparison, never adoption. C6 portability: Linux/WSL2 x86_64 and macOS arm64 install path. Rules: agreement between judges never promotes; only an executed local comparison later promotes to adopted. Dispositions: integrate_now (recommend an integration unit today: name the exact acceptance command a bounded local_integration check would run), targeted_candidate (worth a comparison, name it), keep_but_compare (overlaps an incumbent; name the comparison that would overturn), not_adopted (does not fit; say why), refuted (claims in the evidence did not hold).

The packet claimed instructor 'Overlaps none of the listed agent-SDK/orchestration incumbents directly ... since none of them is named by the catalog as providing typed/validated structured-output extraction' — a catalog-naming test standing in for a capability test. Two listed incumbents already provide exactly instructor's core capability (JSON-Schema-constrained, validated output with a retry-on-validation-failure loop) and provide it on the user's native sign-ins: anthropics/claude-code via the Workflow tool's per-stage `schema:` contract with schema-failure re-ask, in use in this repository at .claude/workflows/layer-verdict-lane.js lines 31-56 (agent(..., { agentType, model, effort, schema: LANE_RETURN }) and schema: VOTE), and openai/codex via `codex exec --output-schema <FILE>` plus `--json` JSONL events on the ChatGPT login. The packet's own proposed narrow fit — 'inside an isolated-builder or evidence-reviewer step that needs typed parsing of an LLM response' — is therefore duplication of the harness those steps already run under. Beyond C5, instructor fails the layer on its own terms: C2 is unmet (the accuracy lens confirmed a real named-hook taxonomy in instructor/v2/core/hooks.py — completion:kwargs/response/usage/error/last_attempt, parse:error — but these are in-process Python callbacks, not a session/event wire protocol; no resumable sessions, no MCP (a repo-wide search returns two non-feature hits, a blog post and a sitemap), and no tool dispatch, only schema-level parallel-tool-call parsing), and C3 is satisfied only vacuously because there is no execution environment to isolate. C1 is better than recorded (a built-in ollama builder with api_key 'ollama' — 'required but unused' — so the paid-key penalty is conditional on hosted-provider arms), and C4 is strong (MIT verified, v1.17.0 2026-09-09 with six releases inside the trailing 6-month window, top-level tests/, .coveragerc, and test/ty/ruff/mutation/package-compatibility CI). Strong C4 and a passable C1 do not rescue a candidate that closes no gap and is not an agent SDK: the maintainers themselves route past it ('Use Instructor for fast extraction, reach for PydanticAI when you need agents'). The interface claim 'no CLI' was also refuted (pyproject.toml [project.scripts] instructor = instructor.cli.cli:app, with jobs/files/usage/batch/docs subcommands) — but that CLI manages OpenAI fine-tuning and batch jobs, not agent exec, so it does not change the verdict.

First, a fabricated quotation: the packet attributes 'GitHub Workflows – Sandboxed execution on issues, pull requests, or schedules' to the README, and the accuracy lens grepped the full 352-line README and found the string absent — the actual text is 'runs it headless on issues, pull requests or a schedule'. That was the packet's only support for a C3 isolation property beyond the self-flagged-unverified Monty claim, so the sandbox half of C3 is unsupported; what remains (a daemon-free library where deterministic code owns effects) is true but trivial. Second, an evidence-scope mismatch that the evidence-first angle has to weight heavily: every worker feature the packet credits — isolated sub-agent runs with separate message history, DelegationStartEvent/DelegationEndEvent with ok/timeout/budget/failed/contained outcomes, max_calls/timeout_seconds/usage_limits/tool_retries bounds — comes from https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/subagents/, i.e. the separate package pydantic_ai_harness in repo pydantic/pydantic-ai-harness (created 2026-03-20, latest v0.33.0 2026-09-22, 912 stars, MIT). The packet's C4 maturity read is of pydantic-ai v2.47.0 while the differentiating worker layer is a pre-1.0 0.x line in a repository the packet never queried and never installed. Third, C1 'api_key_required' is overstated in both directions relative to the preregistered wording ('or a local model'): the same models/overview page the packet lists in sources_read carries Ollama under OpenAI-compatible providers, OpenAI Codex and GitHub Copilot annotated as riding an existing subscription, and the GitHub Copilot page states the token is 'what `gh auth token` prints, or what the Copilot CLI stores after `copilot login`' with 'no token exchange is needed' — which is exactly the GitHub-login reuse the packet declared no provider offers while simultaneously filing it as an unchecked gap. The penalty belongs on the Anthropic/hosted arm only. Fourth, and decisive for the disposition, the fit lens showed the packet's own named comparison is confounded: pydantic-ai ships TypeSafe (Jev) as a first-class provider (pip install 'pydantic-ai-slim[typesafe]', TYPESAFE_API_KEY — a credential this project already holds at $HOME/.config/typesafe/agent-lab.env), so 'pydantic-ai typed output vs typesafe-ai skill' can run both arms on the same backend. It also named the overlap the packet omitted: the sub-agent dispatch surface lands squarely on anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python and openhands/software-agent-sdk, not on the typed-output sliver. I verified the settler exists here — tools/compare/workers/run-arms.mjs takes `run --out DIR --arms A,B,C` and arm C already executed (executed-comparisons.md:57-61, 535). Same-layer overlap with an incumbent and no executed comparison is keep_but_compare by C5, never adoption; agreement among judges does not promote it, and the fabricated-quote finding forecloses integrate_now.

The packet's three stated grounds for a negative fit verdict are all refuted, and I reproduced the refutations against primary source rather than accepting them: (a) packet `interface` ("No headless/exec automation mode was found in the material read; the CLI is described as for interactive prototyping, not scripted dispatch") is refuted at blocking severity — `gh api repos/strands-agents/harness-sdk/contents/strands-cli/README.md` "## Run modes" table gives "**Print** | `--print` is set, or stdin is piped | One request, then exit" and "**ACP server** | `--acp-server` is set | Serve the agent over newline-delimited ACP on stdin/stdout", with `-p, --print`, `--session-id <id>` "Resume a conversation by id", `--mcp-config <path>`, `--skills <dirs>`, `--interventions <policy>` in the Options table; (b) packet `isolation_model` ("No sandbox, container, or worktree isolation model is described") is refuted — `strands-py/src/strands/sandbox/` ships `base.py, docker.py, ssh.py, posix_shell.py, stream_process.py, not_a_sandbox_local_environment.py, types.py, errors.py`, i.e. host-process is the named default, not the only model; (c) packet `native_login_support: api_key_required` as a blanket C1 failure is refuted on C1's explicit "or a local model" limb — `strands-py/src/strands/models/` ships first-party `ollama.py`, `llamacpp.py`, `litellm.py` alongside `anthropic.py/bedrock.py/openai.py/gemini.py`, and the CLI provider table auto-detects `ollama/` and `litellm/` locally with no required key. The blocking refutation disqualifies integrate_now outright. On corrected evidence the genuine gap versus the incumbents is narrow but real: a headless, MCP-aware, skills-aware coding agent that can be pointed at this project's existing local vLLM/Ollama endpoint with no paid key and with pluggable docker/ssh tool sandboxing plus Cedar tool-call gating — neither `claude -p` nor `codex exec` offers a local-model worker path. Against that, the overlap is larger than the packet said and lands on the project's own surface, not only the library axis: the CLI discovers MCP servers from `~/.claude.json` and `.codex/config.toml` and skills from `.claude/skills`/`.codex/skills`, so it duplicates the incumbent worker shape directly. C1 still carries a recorded penalty (no Claude Code / Codex / GitHub / Google sign-in reuse; hosted providers need Anthropic key, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, or the AWS credential chain — substance verified, though the packet cited it to dead `user-guide/concepts/...` URLs). C2 is satisfied on all four limbs; C4 is strong (Apache-2.0, dense per-package CI, five releases 2026-09-15..21) though no CI run status was queried and the harness/CLI packages are v0.1.x; C6 is inferred from Python 3.10+/Node 22+ only. Not "refuted" as a disposition: this is a fit judgement on an evidence packet whose factual defects were corrected, and the corrected facts point at an unmeasured overlap, not a failed product.

claims.claim: Repo strands-agents/harness-sdk is the Strands Agents monorepo: Apache-2.0, ~7,535 stars, 1,183 forks, 789 open issues, pushed 2026-09-22, containing harness-py, harness-ts, strands-py (Python SDK), strands-ts (TypeScript SDK), strands-cli, strands-mcp, and the docs site.

README states: 'Strands Agents is an open-source SDK for building and running AI agents in Python and TypeScript... it runs in your process with no hosted control plane' and covers lifecycle controls (turn limits, token budgets, cancellation, stop reasons), tools, structured output, MCP, multi-agent patterns, memory and sessions, model portability, streaming, guardrails, tracing, and evals.

votes.why: The only repository in this category naming a capability the incumbents demonstrably failed to supply on this host, which is why gap-first ranks it first despite two refuted votes. Both votes returned refuted=true, and I treat their corrections as narrowing the claim rather than removing it. The fit vote's major finding actually IMPROVES C3 against the packet: the packet asserts CAO 'does not by itself give deterministic per-worker filesystem ownership' and calls working_directory a manual workaround, but src/cli_agent_orchestrator/services/worktree_service.py provisions an isolated git worktree on its own branch derived deterministically from the server-generated terminal_id (WORKTREE_SUBDIR '.cao/worktrees', BRANCH_PREFIX 'cao/'), exposed as `use_worktree` on terminal creation per docs/api.md. Its second major finding correctly deflates the packet's C5 headline: cross-vendor orchestration in one run is NOT missing here - docs/tasks/2026-09-21-native-workflow-alignment.md records workflow wf_d9b80dae-35f, stage codex-stage, driving a live Codex process under native ChatGPT login inside a Workflow graph. But that same record is what leaves a genuine gap: the Codex turn aborted at 26.2s (rollout token_count 24,453, turn_aborted reason interrupted), the companion job label stayed 'running' for ~9.5 min until cancel, no result.json was written, and the workspace-keyed broker is torn down by any session's SessionEnd. CAO's counterpart - a journaled workflow run with `--run-id` replay-resume raising ReplayDivergenceError on nondeterminism, plus 'the step's outcome was written server-side before the worker terminal was torn down' with GET /handoff-results/{job_id} returning running/completed/error - addresses exactly that failure class, and no incumbent supplies it. Not integrate_now, for three reasons the votes established: the accuracy vote found the packet fabricated its own schema quotation (the cited docs/event-driven-architecture.md contains no 'no explicit JSON schema' sentence, and no schema/version language at all), found the six orchestration/cross-provider tests are in test/e2e/ which ci.yml excludes via `--ignore=test/e2e -m "not e2e"` with no lane anywhere running them (so the exact capability under consideration is untested in CI), and found two omitted C3 facts - Claude Code is launched with `--dangerously-skip-permissions` by default with a trust-prompt auto-answer fallback, while cao-server auth is opt-in (CAO_AUTH_JWKS_URI/AUTH0_DOMAIN) and an accepted PTY WebSocket 'grants full read/write access to that terminal's PTY, including command input'. An unauthenticated local control plane able to inject commands into agents running with permissions bypassed is not something to integrate before a measured run. Cadence is stronger than the packet recorded (five non-prerelease releases in the window, not one).

rows.resolution: First evidence packet was placeholder text (discarded); re-collected with a fresh packet, two refutation lenses and three judges.

evidence.auth_model: ACP itself defines no fixed auth mechanism; auth is delegated per-agent-implementation. Per docs (agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/schema, "Authentication"): the Agent advertises `authMethods` (each an `AuthMethod` with `id`, `name`, optional `description`) during `initialize`, and if a session cannot be created without auth the Agent returns an `auth_required` error and the Client calls `authenticate` with a chosen method id. Two method shapes exist: "Agent handles authentication itself through `authenticate`. This is the default when no `type` is specified" (`type` omitted/"agent"), or `type: "terminal"` where the "Client runs the configured agent program as a separate interactive process, without passing this method to `authenticate`" — i.e. the client shells out to the underlying agent CLI's own interactive login. This terminal path is exactly how the known official adapters bind ACP to native CLI logins (e.g. `claude-code-acp` delegates to the Claude Code CLI's own subscription login; `codex-acp`-style adapters delegate to Codex/ChatGPT login) rather than ACP mandating an API key.

Transport: "Local agents run as sub-processes of the code editor, communicating via JSON-RPC over stdio." Remote agents "can be hosted in the cloud or on separate infrastructure, communicating over HTTP or WebSocket," but "Full support for remote agents is a work in progress."

Sessions: "Clients create a new session by calling the session/new method with: The working directory for the session, A list of MCP servers the Agent should connect to." Resumability: agents with `loadSession` capability replay the full conversation via session/update notifications on resume; agents advertising `sessionCapabilities.resume` let clients reconnect "without replaying the conversation history."

Structured events: agents report tool invocations via session/update notifications carrying toolCallId, title, kind (read/edit/execute/fetch), status (pending/in_progress/completed/failed), diffs, and terminal output; sensitive actions go through session/request_permission before execution.

Isolation model: terminal/tool execution runs inside the Client's (editor's) own process and environment — "The terminal methods allow Agents to execute shell commands within the Client's environment" and the Client owns the terminal id/lifecycle ("The Client returns a Terminal ID immediately... The Client responds once the command exits"); ACP itself defines no sandbox/container isolation layer, leaving isolation to whatever the Client (editor/host) provides.

MCP integration is explicit and first-class: "Clients MAY include connection details for MCP servers that the Agent should connect to" at session/new, supporting stdio (mandatory), HTTP and SSE transports; the wire format "re-uses the JSON representations used in MCP where possible."

evidence.interface: ACP is a JSON-RPC 2.0 wire protocol, not an SDK you call as a library function per se, though official runtime SDKs (Rust `agent-client-protocol`, TypeScript `@agentclientprotocol/sdk`, Python, Kotlin, Java) implement it. Local agents run as editor subprocesses communicating over stdio; remote agents (still "work in progress" per docs) speak HTTP/WebSocket. Core methods: `initialize` (capability/version negotiation), `authenticate`, `session/new`, `session/load`, `session/prompt`, `session/cancel`, `session/update` (server->client notifications carrying structured tool-call/message events), `session/request_permission`, plus terminal methods (`terminal/create`, `terminal/output`, `terminal/wait_for_exit`, `terminal/kill`, `terminal/release`). This is a headless, event-driven control-plane interface between an editor/client and any coding agent.
evidence.isolation_model: No isolation/sandbox is defined by ACP itself. Tool execution (including terminal commands) runs "within the Client's environment": the Client process owns the actual OS process, working directory and lifecycle (create/output/wait/kill/release), while the Agent only requests actions and receives structured status back. There is no per-session container, VM or worktree concept in the protocol; any sandboxing, per-worktree isolation or "deterministic code owns the effects" guarantee has to come from the specific Client or Agent implementation, not from ACP.
evidence.worker_features: ACP supports concurrent/queued session management (session/new, session/load, session/cancel), resumable sessions via `sessionCapabilities.resume` (reconnect without full history replay) or `loadSession` (full replay), custom tool-call reporting with kind/status/content (text, images, resource blocks, diffs, live terminal output), explicit MCP server wiring per session (stdio/HTTP/SSE), and a permission-request round trip (session/request_permission) so a client can gate risky actions. There is no built-in multi-worker/fan-out orchestration primitive in the protocol itself — dispatch/parallelism is left to the Client or Agent implementation.
evidence.structured_events: session/update notifications are the structured-event channel: they carry tool-call lifecycle updates (toolCallId, human-readable title, kind: read/edit/execute/fetch, status: pending/in_progress/completed/failed), diff content for file edits, live terminal output tied to a terminalId, and agent message/thought chunks. Combined with the JSON Schema published under schema/v1 and schema/v2 in this repo, these events are machine-parseable and versioned, not just log text.
evidence.tests_and_ci: The repository runs upstream CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml) plus a cargo-deny license/dependency-advisory check (deny.yml, deny.toml), automated schema publishing (publish-schema.yml) and registry sync (sync-registry.yml) on every push, orchestrated by an automated release-plz bot that also cuts releases (release-plz.yml). Rust workspace members include the schema crate, schema/v1, schema/v2 and schema-generator, implying the CI exercises schema generation/consistency, though the exact upstream test-command output was not executed in this evidence pass (source_review of workflow file names and workspace layout only, not a run of `cargo test`).

C1: the packet called this 'the strongest C1 fit in the slice — OAuth via the user's existing GitHub login'. It does not reuse an existing sign-in: `grep 'gh auth'` over the README returns zero hits; the server runs its own browser OAuth per process against app credentials baked into the official image and keeps the token in memory only, so an unattended stdio worker re-authorizes on every start and the documented headless paths are a device code, a minted PAT, or a GitHub App private key. Against the incumbent `gh` — already authenticated on this host as seathatflowsinourveins with a gho_ token and repo/workflow/read:org/gist scopes — that is strictly a new credential lifecycle, not zero setup. Separately the packet's blanket 'no paid API key of any kind' overreaches: the Copilot coding-agent dispatch tools require a paid Copilot plan plus Actions minutes and AI credits, and create_pull_request_with_copilot exists only on the hosted remote server. C3: no execution or filesystem sandbox and no per-worktree ownership of GitHub-side effects — the only controls are --read-only, PAT scope, --oauth-scopes filtering and Lockdown Mode, and the README the packet claims to have read end to end states Lockdown Mode is explicitly 'not an authorization boundary' (the packet filed it as unread, so treat its README coverage as partial). C2 is real but thin: stdio, a self-hosted `github-mcp-server http` Streamable-HTTP mode the packet missed, and an in-repo Go library marked unstable; no SDK for a non-Go project. C5: it duplicates `gh` for PR/issue/Actions work, `gh --json`/`--jq` already produces typed output under this project's RTK filtering, and with ~119 tools and no dynamic toolset discovery the packet's 'reduces context' claim runs in an unmeasured direction. C1 fails outright as native-auth fit and is recorded as a penalty, not an exclusion: the packet's auth_model quotes the README ("Sign up at Snyk and get an API token ... export SNYK_TOKEN=your-api-token-here"), and the accuracy lens adds a second, equally non-native path (docs/cli-reference.md line 429, `snyk auth` through a local credential proxy, "required even with --no-upload"); neither is a Claude Code, Codex/ChatGPT, GitHub or Google login nor a local model. C2 is better than the packet stated and is not the blocker: the accuracy lens confirms `--json` with a documented ScanPathResult schema in docs/json-output.md, `--ci` ("Exit non-zero when findings or operational failures remain"), ignore-risk/issue-code flags and an args-from-YAML file, so a bounded check can key on the version-stable exit code and retain the explicitly experimental JSON as an artifact only; there are still no resumable sessions, no custom-tool surface and no MCP server. C3 is where the packet was materially wrong and where fit turns. The packet called this "read-only security auditing ... run as a standalone CLI outside the agent runtime"; the fit lens refutes that from the README's own Security Warning ("Agent Scan starts stdio MCP servers by executing the commands in the config and connects to configured remote MCP server URLs with their configured headers"), and the accuracy lens shows two undocumented-in-README commands, `evo` and `guard`, where `guard install {claude,cursor,codex,github-copilot,all} [--managed]` writes hooks into the host agent's user or MDM-managed configuration and installs a fire-and-forget SessionStart hook emitting `sessionStartServerDiscovery` to api.snyk.io (docs/cli-reference.md; src/agent_scan/guard.py, hooks/, hook_events.py). Two further C3 facts the packet omitted: scan state defaults to `~/.mcp-scan`, home-directory state shared across every worktree, and the documented default invocation is whole-machine discovery. The packet's consent claim also does not hold as stated: consent is scoped to interactive runs, and every way this project would call it (agent Bash, workflow stage, CI) is non-TTY, where remote/http servers are contacted with no prompt and stdio servers are skipped entirely unless `--dangerously-run-mcp-servers` executes the ecosystem wrappers. Deterministic code can still own the effects, but only as an operator-enforced restriction (explicit CONFIG_FILE paths, `--storage-file` in scratch, never `guard install`, MCP arm only inside a container), never as a property of the tool — which is exactly the distinction C3 asks for. C1 penalty stands and is the only disposition-relevant claim that survived unchanged. `SNYK_TOKEN` from a Snyk account (README "Sign up at Snyk ... export SNYK_TOKEN="). The packet's absolute "no native login documented anywhere in the README or file tree" was asserted over a tree it had not read; docs/cli-reference.md line 429 documents a second path, the Snyk CLI extension `snyk agent-scan --experimental` requiring `snyk auth` through a local credential proxy, and line 415 says SNYK_TOKEN is "Required for `scan` unless a push key is configured ... C2 is stronger than the packet claimed, in the packet's favour. The accuracy lens found `--json` with a documented schema in docs/json-output.md (ScanPathResult), `--ci` ("Exit non-zero when findings or operational failures remain"), `--ignore-risk-names`/`--ignore-issues-codes`, args-from-YAML, and a push-key/control-server upload contract. The experimental-schema banner ("risk indicator names, scores, field names, and response structure ... may change without notice") is a stability penalty, not an absence of programmatic control. No resumable sessions, no custom tools, not an MCP server — C2 partial: exit-code-stable, schema-unstable.

C3 is where the packet fails, and both lenses agree with independent citations. Three refuted claims: (a) "CLI only (scan|inspect|help)" and "read-only ... outside the agent runtime" — docs/cli-reference.md documents `evo` and `guard`, and `guard install {claude,cursor,codex,github-copilot,all}` writes hooks into the host agent's user or `--managed` MDM configuration and installs a fire-and-forget SessionStart hook emitting `sessionStartServerDiscovery` to api.snyk.io; src/agent_scan/ carries guard.py, hooks/, hook_events.py. (b) Even `scan` is not read-only: README Security Warning — "Agent Scan starts stdio MCP servers by executing the commands in the config and connects to configured remote MCP server URLs with their configured headers." (c) The consent gate is scoped to interactive runs: "Non-interactive environments ... inspect remote MCP servers automatically. They do not start stdio servers unless --dangerously-run-mcp-servers is set." Every way this project would invoke it (agent Bash call, workflow stage, CI) is non-TTY, so the packet's "interactive per-server y/n consent by default, skipped only for fleet mode" is false for our actual invocation path. Add `--storage-file` defaulting to `~/.mcp-scan` (state outside any worktree, shared across the host) and a documented whole-machine default scan that would egress user-scope configs and skill content for every installed agent. Deterministic code can still own the effects, but only under operator-enforced restrictions (explicit CONFIG_FILE paths, explicit --storage-file, never `guard install`, never `--dangerously-run-mcp-servers` outside a container) — a restriction, not a property of the tool. C3 = conditional, and these are blocking claims refuted, which disqualifies integrate_now under the stated rule.

C5 decides the disposition. The packet's own open_gaps concede "No executed local comparison was run against the project's installed Gitleaks/zizmor/Agent Skills validator".

evidence.summary: Snyk Agent Scan is a Python CLI (`snyk-agent-scan`) that discovers agent harnesses, MCP server configs and agent skills on a machine and scans them for prompt injection, tool poisoning/shadowing, toxic flows, malicious skill code, secret handling and other supply-chain risks, sending redacted component data to the Snyk Agent Scan analysis API (or a self-hosted Snyk Evo instance for fleet/background mode).
evidence.interface: CLI only (`snyk-agent-scan scan|inspect|help [CONFIG_FILE...]`), distributed via `uvx snyk-agent-scan@latest`/`@0.5.17` (PyPI package `snyk-agent-scan`) or standalone signed binaries per-OS/arch from GitHub Releases (with SBOM, checksums, GPG-signed checksums). It is a security scanner over MCP/skill configs, not an SDK for building MCP servers or agents, and not itself an MCP server (source_review: README Quick Start / CLI Parameters sections).
evidence.auth_model: Requires a Snyk account and API token set as `SNYK_TOKEN` env var, obtained from https://app.snyk.io/account (source_review: README 'Before using either option' steps 1-2, quoted: 'Sign up at Snyk and get an API token ... Set the token as an environment variable before running any scan: export SNYK_TOKEN=your-api-token-here'). Background/MDM 'push-key' fleet mode reports to a Snyk Evo instance and is contact-sales gated. No use of Claude Code, Codex/ChatGPT, GitHub or Google native login is documented anywhere in the README or file tree; this is a separate paid Snyk credential, which C1 records as a penalty rather than an exclusion.
evidence.isolation_model: Runs as a local process against the caller's discovered agent config files; scanning MCP configs can execute stdio server commands and make outbound network requests to configured remote MCP URLs. The README explicitly recommends running scans "inside a sandbox (Docker container, VM, or disposable environment)" for untrusted configs, gates server contact behind an interactive per-server y/n consent prompt by default (declined servers get `user_declined` and are never contacted), and only skips consent for background/push-key fleet scans, which still do not start stdio servers unless `--dangerously-run-mcp-servers` is passed (source_review: README 'Security Warning' and 'Interactive Consent for MCP Servers' sections). It also applies SSRF-style guards, refusing remote MCP requests to link-local/cloud-metadata ranges (169.254.0.0/16, fe80::/10, fd00:ec2::254, 100.100.100.200), not following redirects, though it notes a DNS-rebinding window between initial DNS validation and connection time (source_review: README, same section). This is caller-provided process isolation guidance (Docker/VM), not a sandbox the tool itself provides.
evidence.worker_features: Not an orchestration/dispatch SDK; "worker" features here are scanner concepts: two run modes (interactive foreground Scan Mode producing a one-shot report, and Background/MDM Mode that scans on regular intervals and reports centrally to Snyk Evo for fleet-wide monitoring). No custom-tool/dispatch or multi-agent worker API is documented (source_review: README 'Scanner Capabilities' section).
evidence.structured_events: v0.6+ emits a "risk-based" scored report format against a versioned analysis API (2026-07-10); v0.5.x emits an issue-code based format against the 2025-09-02 API. Both output schemas are explicitly marked experimental/unstable: README quotes "The raw output of this CLI — including risk indicator names, scores, field names, and response structure — is experimental and may change without notice between releases. We do not recommend building production workflows that depend on specific CLI output fields or risk names" (source_review: README banner). No mention of resumable sessions or a documented event-stream/webhook contract for the local CLI itself; background mode's reporting contract into Snyk Evo is not detailed in this repo's README.
evidence.tests_and_ci: Repo contains a tests/ tree with unit, e2e, canary_specs, mcp_servers, skills, v4compatibility subdirectories and a test_configs.json, plus a demoserver directory and .pre-commit-config.yaml; CI is configured via GitHub Actions at .github/workflows/tests.yml and there is also a .circleci directory present, indicating dual/legacy CI configuration (source_review: `gh api repos/snyk/agent-scan/contents` tree listing and `.github/workflows` listing). Workflow contents and pass/fail status were not read in this pass (open gap).
evidence.maintenance: Active: repo pushed 2026-09-22T11:23:51Z (same day as this evaluation), 3,079 stargazers, 278 forks, 13 open issues, weekly-or-faster release cadence (v0.6.3 to v0.6.4 in ~11 days with intermediate snapshot builds), maintained by Snyk org with a named release author account. Created 2025-04-07 (source_review: `gh api repos/snyk/agent-scan` repo metadata and releases listing).
evidence.portability: Standalone binaries published per-OS/arch on GitHub Releases (linux-arm64 build observed in release asset names) alongside SBOM and GPG-signed checksums; also installable via uvx (Python, requires uv) from PyPI package snyk-agent-scan, which is platform-agnostic wherever Python/uv runs, covering Linux/WSL2 x86_64 and macOS arm64 in principle. The README's OS support matrix ("Supported agents and capabilities") documents scanning coverage separately for macOS/Linux/Windows per host agent (Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, Copilot, Gemini CLI, Codex, etc.), confirming Linux and macOS are both first-class scan targets (source_review: README Quick Start and 'Supported agents and capabilities' table). Exact linux-x86_64 and macos-arm64 binary asset filenames were not individually confirmed in this pass beyond the linux-arm64 sample seen (open gap).
evidence.fit_with_native_workflow: Directly relevant to the project's MCP/agent-skill supply-chain posture: it auto-discovers Claude Code (and Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code, Copilot, Gemini CLI, Codex, Windsurf, Kiro, OpenCode, Antigravity, Amazon Q, Amp, OpenClaw) MCP configs and skills at system/user/project/extension scope and screens them for prompt injection, tool poisoning/shadowing, toxic flows, secret handling and malicious skill code before those components are trusted in-session. It does not replace or provide an MCP SDK, gateway or A2A/ACP protocol implementation for this project's own tool-building work; its role is read-only security auditing of already-installed agent components, run as a standalone CLI outside the agent runtime, and it introduces a separate Snyk account/API-key dependency (not one of the project's native logins) plus outbound network calls to Snyk's analysis API unless self-hosted via Evo.
evidence.overlap_with_incumbents: The project already runs Gitleaks (guarded, for secret scanning) and zizmor (for GitHub Actions workflow security) per docs/native-upstream-additions.md, and the Agent Skills reference validator mentioned there may already cover some skill-manifest checks; those tools do not cover MCP tool-poisoning/prompt-injection/toxic-flow analysis or agent-skill malicious-code/prompt-injection scanning that agent-scan targets, so this is a distinct capability rather than a duplicate of the installed secret/workflow scanners.
risks: Requires a separate Snyk account and paid/free-tier API token (SNYK_TOKEN) rather than any native Claude/Codex/GitHub/Google login — an external credential dependency and potential cost/ToS surface (agreeing to Snyk's Agent Scan terms of use is required per the README).

Scanning MCP configs can execute stdio server commands and issue outbound network requests as a side effect of the scan itself; interactive consent and SSRF guards mitigate but do not eliminate this (README notes an unresolved DNS-rebinding window between validation and connection time).

Component data (agent details, MCP server configs/signatures, tool names/descriptions, skill content) is sent to Snyk's analysis API for scoring; secrets are redacted before transmission per the README, but this is still third-party data egress for anyone running the scan against this project's configs unless self-hosted Evo is used.

Both v0.5.x and v0.6.x output schemas are explicitly marked experimental and may change without notice, so any acceptance/automation built on parsed CLI output would need to tolerate breaking format changes across releases.
v0.5.x is stated as 'planned for deprecation', so any integration should target v0.6+.

findings.claim: fit_with_native_workflow: "its role is read-only security auditing of already-installed agent components, run as a standalone CLI outside the agent runtime"
findings.problem: Not read-only. The scanner's core mechanism is to start stdio MCP servers by executing the commands in the discovered config and to connect to remote MCP URLs with their configured headers. The packet's own isolation_model and risks[] say this, so the fit field contradicts the packet's own evidence and would let a C3 reviewer score isolation on a false premise. On this host the effect is concrete: .mcp.json declares serena and socraticode as stdio servers launched through $HOME/.local/share/codex-ecosystem/bin wrappers (socraticode carrying an env block with local Qdrant/vLLM endpoints) and ai-memory as an http server on 127.0.0.1:49374, so a scan either executes those wrappers or is blind to their tool descriptions.
findings.evidence: README 'Security Warning' (fetched 2026-09-22 via gh api repos/snyk/agent-scan/readme, saved at <session-scratchpad>): "To retrieve tool descriptions, Agent Scan starts stdio MCP servers by executing the commands in the config and connects to configured remote MCP server URLs with their configured headers." Local config: $HOME/code/agent-lab/.mcp.json.

findings.claim: isolation_model: server contact is "gated behind an interactive per-server y/n consent prompt by default" and "only skips consent for background/push-key fleet scans"
findings.problem: The README scopes the consent gate to interactive runs and drops it for any non-interactive environment, not only contact-sales fleet mode. Every way this project would invoke the tool - an agent Bash call, a workflow stage, a CI step - is non-TTY, so the default there is: remote/http MCP servers are contacted automatically with no prompt, and stdio servers are not started at all unless --dangerously-run-mcp-servers is passed. Neither branch is what the packet describes: the useful MCP arm on this host (serena, socraticode tool descriptions) is unreachable non-interactively without the dangerous flag, which also removes consent for the loopback http server. This changes the C3 answer and the shape of any acceptance command.
findings.evidence: README 'Interactive Consent for MCP Servers': "By default, Agent Scan prompts for user consent before contacting each discovered MCP server during interactive runs" and "Non-interactive environments (e.g., background and push-key scans) inspect remote MCP servers automatically. They do not start stdio servers unless --dangerously-run-mcp-servers is set." CLI Parameters: "--dangerously-run-mcp-servers  Skip consent and contact all configured MCP servers".

findings.claim: isolation_model: "Runs as a local process against the caller's discovered agent config files", offered as the C3 answer with no mention of persistent or machine-wide state
findings.problem: Two C3-relevant facts are missing. (a) Scan state is kept in a home-directory file by default - "--storage-file FILE  Path to store scan state (default: ~/.mcp-scan)" - hidden global state outside any worktree and shared across every scan on the host. (b) The documented default invocation is whole-machine, which on this host would discover and ship user-scope configs and skill content for every supported agent (Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, Cursor, VS Code, OpenCode, Antigravity) to the Snyk analysis API, not just this repository's components. Ownership by deterministic code is achievable, but only by passing explicit CONFIG_FILE paths plus --storage-file; the packet never states that, so C3 as answered overstates containment.
findings.evidence: README 'CLI Parameters': "--storage-file FILE  Path to store scan state (default: ~/.mcp-scan)", "--scan-all-users  Scan all readable user home directories"; README Quick Start: "# Scan the whole machine / uvx snyk-agent-scan@latest"; README 'Analysis and Validation': component info incl. "MCP server configurations and signatures, tool names and descriptions, and skill content" is sent to the API.

Treat the MCP arm as a separate, separately bounded comparison, not part of that check: non-interactively it reaches only the loopback ai-memory http server and skips serena and socraticode entirely, so obtaining tool descriptions requires --dangerously-run-mcp-servers, which executes the ecosystem wrapper commands with their env and removes consent for the http server.
